characterized_levers.name: Technical Feasibility Strategy
characterized_levers.consequences: Demonstrating technical feasibility impacts policy. Immediate: Demonstrators built → Systemic: 15% increased policy traction due to concrete evidence → Strategic: Enhanced credibility in procurement negotiations.
options: Focus demonstrator efforts on a single, highly secure authentication method, such as FIDO2, on a mainstream Android device.
Develop demonstrators for both FIDO2 on GrapheneOS and a browser-based fallback, accepting slightly longer development timelines.
Explore passwordless authentication via blockchain-anchored identity and decentralized identifiers (DIDs) alongside FIDO2 and browser-based fallback demonstrators.
characterized_levers.review: Controls Technical Risk vs. Scope. Weakness: The options don't explicitly address the cost implications of each demonstrator approach.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: This lever focuses on demonstrating technical feasibility to impact policy, quantifying the impact. It is distinct because it quantifies the impact of the technical demonstrators on policy traction, unlike other levers. It also has specific options related to demonstrator development.
characterized_levers.description: The Technical Feasibility Strategy lever focuses on demonstrating that platform-neutral and fallback-capable digital identity solutions are technically viable. It controls the scope and direction of the technical demonstrator work, aiming to produce credible evidence that alternatives to the Apple/Google duopoly exist. Key success metrics include the completion of two working demonstrators (mobile and fallback) and the inclusion of technical findings in the feasibility report. The objective is to de-risk the policy and procurement interventions.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: This lever strongly supports the Policy Advocacy Strategy (80b177d0-c67e-4bc2-bd50-3f49b815e633) by providing concrete evidence to support policy proposals. It also enhances the Procurement Influence Strategy (f1c0d856-0cfc-4def-ab68-c58bb8b17551) by showcasing viable alternatives.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: A narrow technical focus can conflict with the Coalition Building Strategy (1731ad9a-c471-40de-9b90-12f23721aebd) if the chosen solutions are not broadly acceptable. Overly ambitious technical goals may also constrain the EU Standards Engagement Strategy (2e9016aa-8563-447e-a5e0-0e146f4ebad3) by diverting resources.

characterized_levers.name: Policy Advocacy Strategy
characterized_levers.consequences: Policy advocacy shapes procurement. Immediate: Policy proposals submitted → Systemic: 20% greater likelihood of influencing AltID requirements → Strategic: Increased adoption of platform-neutral standards.
options: Focus advocacy on continuity of service and supplier concentration risks, avoiding direct privacy arguments.
Balance continuity arguments with privacy and democratic accountability concerns, broadening the coalition.
Prioritize open-source governance and community-led development models for digital identity, framing platform neutrality as a public good.
characterized_levers.review: Controls Political Risk vs. Coalition Size. Weakness: The options don't consider the potential for regulatory capture by incumbent vendors.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: This lever focuses on policy advocacy shaping procurement, quantifying the impact. It is distinct because it quantifies the impact of policy advocacy on influencing AltID requirements, unlike other levers. It also has specific options related to advocacy focus.
characterized_levers.description: The Policy Advocacy Strategy lever shapes the narrative around platform neutrality and fallback access. It controls the arguments presented to Digitaliseringsstyrelsen and other stakeholders, aiming to reframe the issue as one of resilience, continuity, and supplier concentration rather than solely privacy. Success is measured by securing a formal response to the project's proposal and influencing AltID-related policy documents. The objective is to create a favorable policy environment for platform-neutral solutions.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: This lever works in synergy with the Coalition Building Strategy (1731ad9a-c471-40de-9b90-12f23721aebd), as a broader coalition strengthens the advocacy position. It also benefits from the Technical Feasibility Strategy (bd43cd39-f2f0-4358-9f5b-e4dbfdccc474), which provides evidence to support policy claims.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: Focusing too narrowly on continuity may conflict with the EU Standards Engagement Strategy (2e9016aa-8563-447e-a5e0-0e146f4ebad3) if EU standards prioritize other aspects like privacy. Strong advocacy positions may also constrain the Procurement Influence Strategy (f1c0d856-0cfc-4def-ab68-c58bb8b17551) if they are perceived as too radical.

characterized_levers.name: Coalition Building Strategy
characterized_levers.consequences: Coalition strength amplifies advocacy. Immediate: Stakeholder engagement increased → Systemic: 30% stronger advocacy position in procurement discussions → Strategic: Greater political pressure for platform neutrality.
options: Build a narrow coalition focused on security experts and contingency-planning stakeholders.
Expand the coalition to include civil-society organizations, privacy advocates, and academic researchers.
Actively recruit dissenting voices from within the MitID operator and Digitaliseringsstyrelsen to foster internal debate.
characterized_levers.review: Controls Speed vs. Breadth of Support. Weakness: The options fail to address the potential for conflicting priorities within the coalition.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: This lever focuses on coalition building to amplify advocacy, quantifying the impact. It is distinct because it quantifies the impact of coalition strength on advocacy position, unlike other levers. It also has specific options related to coalition composition.
characterized_levers.description: The Coalition Building Strategy lever focuses on assembling a diverse group of stakeholders to support the project's goals. It controls the breadth and depth of stakeholder engagement, aiming to create political pressure for platform neutrality. Success is measured by the strength of the advocacy position in procurement discussions and the overall political support for the project. The objective is to create a united front that amplifies the project's message.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: This lever amplifies the Policy Advocacy Strategy (80b177d0-c67e-4bc2-bd50-3f49b815e633) by providing a broader base of support for policy proposals. It also strengthens the Procurement Influence Strategy (f1c0d856-0cfc-4def-ab68-c58bb8b17551) by increasing political pressure on procurement decisions.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: Building a broad coalition can conflict with the Technical Feasibility Strategy (bd43cd39-f2f0-4358-9f5b-e4dbfdccc474) if diverse stakeholders have conflicting technical preferences. A large coalition may also constrain the EU Standards Engagement Strategy (2e9016aa-8563-447e-a5e0-0e146f4ebad3) if internal disagreements hinder a unified EU advocacy position.

characterized_levers.name: Procurement Influence Strategy
characterized_levers.consequences: Procurement influence drives adoption. Immediate: Platform-neutral language included in procurement documents → Systemic: 25% faster scaling through mandated supplier diversity → Strategic: Reduced long-term dependency on Apple and Google.
options: Focus on including general language about supplier concentration risk in AltID procurement documents.
Advocate for specific requirements for platform-neutral access and certified fallback authentication paths.
Propose a 'digital sovereignty bonus' in procurement scoring, rewarding vendors who demonstrably reduce platform dependency.
characterized_levers.review: Controls Specificity vs. Implementability. Weakness: The options don't account for the potential for vendors to game the procurement process.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: This lever focuses on procurement influence driving adoption, quantifying the impact. It is distinct because it quantifies the impact of procurement influence on scaling, unlike other levers. It also has specific options related to procurement language.
characterized_levers.description: The Procurement Influence Strategy lever aims to incorporate platform-neutrality and fallback access requirements into AltID procurement documents. It controls the specificity and enforceability of these requirements, aiming to reduce long-term dependency on Apple and Google. Success is measured by the inclusion of relevant language in official procurement documents and the resulting supplier diversity. The objective is to create a market incentive for platform-neutral solutions.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: This lever is enabled by the Technical Feasibility Strategy (bd43cd39-f2f0-4358-9f5b-e4dbfdccc474), which demonstrates the viability of platform-neutral solutions. It is also strengthened by the Policy Advocacy Strategy (80b177d0-c67e-4bc2-bd50-3f49b815e633), which creates a favorable policy environment for procurement interventions.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: Demanding highly specific requirements may conflict with the Coalition Building Strategy (1731ad9a-c471-40de-9b90-12f23721aebd) if some stakeholders prefer a more flexible approach. Aggressive procurement language may also constrain the EU Standards Engagement Strategy (2e9016aa-8563-447e-a5e0-0e146f4ebad3) if it clashes with broader EU interoperability goals.

characterized_levers.name: EU Standards Engagement Strategy
characterized_levers.consequences: EU standards engagement creates broader impact. Immediate: Input provided to relevant EU bodies → Systemic: 10% increased alignment with European Digital Identity Wallet requirements → Strategic: Enhanced interoperability and reduced lock-in across Europe.
options: Monitor relevant EU bodies and technical working groups, providing occasional input on interoperability.
Actively engage with EU bodies, advocating for platform-neutral access and certified fallback mechanisms in eIDAS2 and related standards.
Champion a 'sovereign identity sandbox' within the EU Digital Identity Wallet framework to test and validate platform-neutral authentication models.
characterized_levers.review: Controls Resource Allocation vs. Scope of Influence. Weakness: The options don't address the potential for EU standards to be influenced by large platform vendors.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: This lever focuses on EU standards engagement creating broader impact, quantifying the impact. It is distinct because it quantifies the impact of EU standards engagement on alignment with European Digital Identity Wallet requirements, unlike other levers. It also has specific options related to EU engagement strategies.
characterized_levers.description: The EU Standards Engagement Strategy lever focuses on influencing European Digital Identity Wallet standards to support platform-neutral access and fallback mechanisms. It controls the level of engagement with relevant EU bodies, aiming to enhance interoperability and reduce lock-in across Europe. Success is measured by the alignment of Danish advocacy with broader European requirements and the inclusion of relevant language in EU standards. The objective is to create a supportive regulatory environment at the European level.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: This lever benefits from the Policy Advocacy Strategy (80b177d0-c67e-4bc2-bd50-3f49b815e633), which provides a strong policy foundation for EU engagement. It also aligns with the Procurement Influence Strategy (f1c0d856-0cfc-4def-ab68-c58bb8b17551) by promoting standards that support platform-neutral procurement practices.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: Active EU engagement may conflict with the Technical Feasibility Strategy (bd43cd39-f2f0-4358-9f5b-e4dbfdccc474) if demonstrator work lags behind EU standards development. A strong EU focus may also constrain the Coalition Building Strategy (1731ad9a-c471-40de-9b90-12f23721aebd) if it diverts resources from domestic stakeholder engagement.
